title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 39–41): Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, purely order-theoretic framework for 'figures' in his 1986 Analysis situs notes. The axioms are called At 1 – At 7 and involve two relations, ≤ and ≪. (𝔉, ≤) is a poset in which every family that has an upper bound has a supremum and in which there is a least element ∅_𝔉 (At 1). M is the set of irreducible elements. Here this means completely join-irreducible: F is irreducible if, whenever F = sup F_i for a family below F, some F_i already equals F. Since F is not the sup of the empty family, ∅_𝔉 is not irreducible. X ◁ F means X ∈ M and X ≤ F.

Page 40 finishes a check started on p.39. Let 𝔉' be a closed part of 𝔉, i.e. a down-set. Then 𝔉' is bounded-complete, the inclusion 𝔉' → 𝔉 preserves sups, and irreducibility is the same whether computed in 𝔉 or in 𝔉': the families below F and their sups coincide.

- **At 2 is inherited.** At 2 says every F is the sup of F̃ = {X ∈ M | X ≤ F}, i.e. the irreducibles generate everything by joins. For F ∈ 𝔉', the set F̃ is the same in 𝔉 and in 𝔉', and the sup taken in 𝔉 is also the sup in 𝔉'. So down-sets inherit At 2.
- **Definition (spacious).** A closed part 𝔉' is 'spacieuse' if it is stable under arbitrary sups. That is, any family in 𝔉' that has a sup in 𝔉 has that sup in 𝔉'. Every down-set is automatically closed under the sups that are bounded *inside* 𝔉', so spaciousness is a strictly stronger condition.
- **Example 𝔉 = 𝔓(I) with inclusion.** This satisfies At 1–At 3, and M is the set of singletons {i}, carrying the discrete order. A nonempty down-set 𝔉' ⊂ 𝔓(I) is exactly an abstract simplicial complex on I, with vertex set I' = 𝔉' ∩ M, when I is finite. For infinite I one restricts to down-sets of finite subsets. 𝔉' is spacious iff a union of simplices is again a simplex. Then 𝔉' has a largest element I', so 𝔉' = 𝔓(I'), a full simplex.
- **Lesson.** Grothendieck exclaims 'c'est pas du tout pareil !'. General closed parts (simplicial complexes) are far richer than spacious ones (full simplices).
- **Margin note.** He suggests avoiding the word 'spacieux', because 'suffisamment spacieux' / 'très spacieux' are used elsewhere.
- **Where this leads (p.41).** The spacious sub-objects are classified: F' ↦ F' ∩ M is a bijection onto Ferm(M), the down-sets of M, with inverse M' ↦ Env(M') = {F | F̃ ⊂ M'}. This is a Birkhoff-type correspondence.
errors: Minor slip: 'car si F ∈ 𝔉' should be read as F ∈ 𝔉' (the image seems to have 𝔉', so possibly only a transcription issue).

The simplicial-complex identification is stated loosely. One needs 𝔉' nonempty (i.e. ∅ ∈ 𝔉'). For infinite I, only down-sets consisting of finite subsets correspond to simplicial complexes. Grothendieck flags the latter himself.

ideas.what: Down-sets (closed parts) of a bounded-complete poset inherit bounded sups, the set of completely join-irreducibles, and join-generation by irreducibles
ideas.modern_name: Order ideals / lower sets in bounded-complete posets; completely join-irreducible elements; join-density (spatial-type condition)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard lattice/order theory (Birkhoff; Gierz et al., Continuous Lattices and Domains)

ideas.what: 'Spacious' closed parts: down-sets stable under all sups existing in the ambient poset; classified on p.41 by down-sets of M (Birkhoff-type duality)
ideas.modern_name: Down-sets closed under existing joins (principal-ideal-like / complete sub-join-semilattice ideals); Birkhoff representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1937); Raney (1952) for completely distributive / join-generated cases

ideas.what: Abstract simplicial complexes on I as nonempty down-sets of 𝔓(I); spacious ones are exactly full simplices 𝔓(I')
ideas.modern_name: Abstract simplicial complex as an order ideal in the Boolean lattice

missed.claim: The broader axiom system At 1–At 7 uses a pair of relations ≤ and ≪ on a bounded-complete poset of 'figures', with join-generation by irreducible 'figures élémentaires'. This is closely parallel to Scott/domain-theoretic structures (bounded-complete domains, way-below relation, bases of compact/irreducible elements). The parallel is apparently never noted in discussions of Grothendieck's tame-topology project. This page itself only does routine order theory.
missed.quote: Supposons que 𝔉 satisfasse At 2 : ∀F ∈ 𝔉, on a F = sup_{X∈F̃} X où F̃ = {X ∈ M | X ≤ F}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could situate Grothendieck's axiomatic 'analysis situs' within domain theory and pointless topology, but this is speculative and depends on what ≪ means in later pages.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine order-theoretic verifications plus a standard example (simplicial complexes as down-sets of a power set). The only interest is documentary: it shows Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatization of figures and his terminological hesitation over 'spacieux'.
transcription_corrections: 'Alors 𝔉' y satisfait aussi, car si F ∈ 𝔉' ' – the condition is F ∈ 𝔉', not F ∈ 𝔉.
Definition line should read 'La partie fermée 𝔉' de 𝔉 est dite spacieuse' (the prime is on the first 𝔉; a word after it is crossed out).
Axiom labels on this page read 'At 1, At 2, At 3' (consistent with p.41), whereas p.39 has 'Ab'.
'(ici ... = ... discret)' likely reads '(ici ensemble ordonné discret)', i.e. M = singletons with discrete order.

Margin, approximately: 'On dira familles fermées "spacieuses" si stables par Sup' followed by 'Remarques. Il vaudrait mieux éviter le mot "spacieux", à cause de l'emploi de "suffisamment spacieux", "très spacieux"'.
